description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope IOM Ethiopia’s Migration Management and Government (MMG) Unit works closely with the Government of Ethiopia, and various stakeholders to contribute to addressing the migration governnance needs, as well as to promote and uphold the rights of individuals and their communities. The Unit has three main areas of intervention: Coordination and Capacity Development support (CCD), Immigration and border governance (IBG), and Labor Mobility and Social Inclusion (LMI). IOM’ Ethiopia Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion programme provides policy, regulatory and operational guidance in matters related to labour and human mobility facilitation, integration and social cohesion, and diaspora engagement as an enabler of sustainable development in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. description: Background JOB DESCRIPTION UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women Ethiopia Country Office has been implementing four (4) phases of the project “Strengthening institutional capacity of duty-bearers and empowering rights-holders for advancement of gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) in Ethiopia” through support from the Government of Ireland, International Development Programme. The project started in 2021 and will end in January 2027 with the completion of Phase IV extension. The project is fully aligned with the UN Women Strategic Note (2021-2025) and Strategic Note (2026-2030) which is derived from and contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSCDF 2020-2025), and UNSDCF (2025-2030) which outlines the United Nation’s vision and strategic focus in Ethiopia. The overall goal of the project is to strengthen institutional capacity of duty-bearers and empower rights-holders to further advance gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) to promote cohesive, just, inclusive, and democratic society in Ethiopia with four outcomes, Outcome 1: Improved multi-sectoral coordination mechanism and favorable policy environment to respond to violence against women and girls and HTPs in development and humanitarian settings Outcome 2: Women’s representation and participation in leadership is increased, and public offices, democratic institutions and women’s rights organisations are empowered to advance gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) Outcome 3: More women, including young women, meaningfully and effectively participate in peace building processes including through an enabling environment that supports key government stakeholders and women’s rights organizations to promote the women, peace and security (WPS) agenda and Outcome 4: A comprehensive national policy framework on GEWE in place and effectively implemented through strengthened accountability mechanisms and enhanced engagement of women’s rights organizations The first outcome aims to strengthen functional multi-sectoral coordination mechanism in place to respond to violence against women and girls (EVAWG) and harmful traditional practices (HTPs) and enhance capacity of institutions (health justice, and social sector) to providing quality, coordinated and accessible essential services to women and girl’s survivors of violence in accordance with global essential services package. The second outcome focuses on enhancing women’s representation and participation in politics and electoral processes. The third outcome aims to increase the number of women, including young women, meaningfully and effectively participate in peace building processes, through an enabling environment that supports key government stakeholders and women rights organizations to promote the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Agenda. The fourth outcome aims for a comprehensive national policy framework on GEWE, which is effectively implemented through strengthened accountability mechanisms and enhanced engagement of women’s rights organizations. These interventions were implemented with a range of government and CSOs at the Federal level and in selected regional states, including through grants. As the project timeframe is ending in January 2027, an independent final evaluation is planned to be undertaken as per the Project Document. The overall objective of the evaluation is to assess the overall results and the relevance, and efficiency of the project as well as its sustainability and high-level result, both intended and unintended. It also aims to identify successes and challenges of the project’s implementation. In addition, the final evaluation will also have a forward-looking focus and will aim to provide key recommendations for the implementation and scaling up opportunities of future work, based on the lessons learned identified through this evaluation by proposing opportunities for a potential additional phase of the project post 2027 and the approaches to be followed for a long-term project moving forward. The evaluation is expected to follow a participatory approach that will include consultations with key stakeholders including implementing partners, Government partners and community members. The UN Women Ethiopia Country Office is seeking to contract a national consultant to conduct an endline evaluation of Phase I-IV of the project. The evaluation should follow the guiding documents for evaluation at UN Women, including the Evaluation Policy , Evaluation Chapter of the Programme and Operation Manual (POM ), the Global Evaluation Reports, Assessment and Analysis System ( GERAAS) evaluation report quality checklis

title: Disability and Inclusion Consultant
description: Application Closing Date 6th of November Context of Role WISH 2 (Women’s Integrated Sexual Health) is one of three components of the overarching WISH Dividend programme that is being procured by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO). This programme is central to delivering the UK’s priorities on empowering women and girls as set out in the International Development Strategy, the UK’s strategic approach to sub-Saharan Africa and the International Women and Girls Strategy. IPPF is the prime contractor on Lot 2 – Eastern and Southern Africa covering the following countries: Burundi, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Zambia. During the implementation years, the WISH2 program will ensure that transformative approaches for disability inclusion are mainstreamed throughout the programme and national healthcare systems. Role Purpose The consultant will provide technical support to the WISH2 programme, with a focus on accelerating the implementation of WISH2 disability and inclusion strategy especially, policy and systems interventions across the WISH2 countries. The consultant will provide tailored support to WISH2 consortium partners, Organisations of People with Disabilities (OPDs), and accountability mechanisms at country level. Technical Assistance (TA) will focus on capacity building, course correction, capitalization and sustainability of interventions across outputs, strengthening mainstreaming of disability inclusion in healthcare systems. Deliverables Through tailored technical assistance, the consultant will support the following key activities. The consultant will: Guide the multi-stakeholder reflection on findings from the recently concluded disability marker (self-assessment), and document lessons learned. Review the facility disability audit findings, prioritised disability inclusion activities and provide comprehensive recommendations for course correction, scaling, capitalisation and institutionalisation of adopted disability inclusive approaches. Review the OPD capacity assessment data, develop a capacity building framework adapted to needs and contextual considerations, and enable cross-country learning and exchange. Support the design and implementation of the OPD sub-granting mechanism including reviewing proposals, contributing to developing Technical Assistance Agreement (TAA), and providing tailored TA at implementation phase. Collaborate with the WISH2 MERL team on the disability research and learning agendas, including disability measurement study, and contributing to development and review of learning products. Review national policy/strategic priorities identified in country workplans and Country Policy Overview and Engagement plans (CPOEP) and provide TA to ensure they are progressing and aligned to the latest evidence, best practices and inclusive health systems strengthening approaches. Building on the already established OPD database and relationships, establish a community of practice for WISH2 ESA, to facilitate learning, amplify voices and bolster empowerment among OPDs, CSOs and partners. Review the safeguarding pilot model for Zambia to strengthen inclusion of people with disabilities and their needs in the model guideline, training materials, and implementation phase. Tools and approaches The Consultant Will Adapt And Apply WISH2’s Tools And Approaches To Meet Programme Goals. WISH2’s Disability Inclusion Strategy Puts Disability Rights Across All Its Work And Promotes Safe, Inclusive Conditions And Meaningful Participation Within Healthcare Systems. It Uses a Twin-track Approach Mainstreaming: build disability inclusion into all policies, programming and service delivery, so people with disabilities can access and benefit from SRH services. Targeted interventions: address specific physical and attitudinal barriers through tailored SBC outreach, accessible SRH information, reasonable accommodation, assistive support, and involvement of organisations of persons with disabilities (OPDs). Tools such as the Disability Inclusion Marker and Disability Audit tools will be adapted to each country, including humanitarian settings, in consultation with WISH2 staff and national stakeholders. For each new task/assignment, a new work order will be prepared. The total number of days will not exceed 60 days over the 5-month duration of the framework contract. description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.
